newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst sees higher oper profit in 97.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst sees higher oper profit in 97.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Hoechst AG said on Friday that it expects its 1997 operating profit to be slightly above last year's levels, growing at a single-digit rate.
"1997 operating earnings are expected to be slightly better on a comparable basis," management board chairman Juergen Dormann told journalists on the fringes of a summer drinks party.

Dormann said the growth would be in single digits, without being specific, stressing that the forecast was based on comparable numbers for 1996. Hoechst has significantly changed its structure over the last year.
Dormann also said group volume sales would be improved in 1997 than in 1996.
Looking ahead to the second half of the year, he said it would be better than the second half of 1996 but not better than the first half of 1997.
In 1996, Hoechst posted earnings which largely disappointed investors, particularly as the company presented an unexpected fourth quarter loss.
Reasons for the improvement included improved currency exchange rates, Dormann said.
In addition in the first four to five months of the year, sales at the group's HMR drugs unit grew about six percent, Dormann said.
Hoechst's crop protection business, AgrEvo, jointly owned with Schering AG also showed particularly strong growth in sales, outstripping pharmaceuticals sales, while earnings topped expectations.
"AgrEvo performed better than planned, largely due to new products and also improved currency relationships," Dormann said.
Hoechst's specialty chemicals group also fared very well, largely because of restructuring benefits and improved economic conditions.
Reinhard Handte, managing director of specialty chemicals unit Clariant GmbH, of which Hoechst owns 45 percent, said that some price hikes could be possible in this segment.
Hoechst sold its specialty chemicals busioness to Swiss bourse listed group Clariant last year.
Hoechst will becaome a strategic management holding company on July 1, when it will be no longer directly involved in any operational activities.
